newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian unions to picket Renault plant in France.
newsitem.headline: Belgian unions to picket Renault plant in France.

text.p: Belgian unions plan to take their protest against the closure of French car maker Renault SA's Belgian plant across the border into France on Wednesday, where they will picket Renault's Douai plant.

"500 of us will head in the direction of Renault Douai early tomorrow morning where we will be present at change of shifts and ask for solidarity," Karel Gacoms of the CMB metal workers union told Reuters on Tuesday.

On Thursday unions expect Renault chief executive officer Louis Schweitzer to attend a works council meeting at Renault Industrie Belgique (RIB) in Vilvoorde after attending a similar meeting at the Renault Group in Paris, he said.
Unions at all Belgian car assembly plants are calling for a one-hour stoppage at each shift on Friday. The halt will affect production at Volvo, Volkswagen, Ford, Opel and Renault.
The action will coincide with similar stoppages at Renault plants in France and Spain. Belgian unions are still discussing such action in Portugal and Slovenia.
Members of all Belgian unions will participate in a March For Jobs on Sunday, March 16, Gacoms said. The location of the march has yet to be announced.
Renault announced the surprise closure of its Belgian plant on February 27, sparking anger among unions and politicians at the loss of 3,100 jobs.
